notes: The 'picture' is two labelled rectangles ('box', 'toy'), so a K-age pre-reader cannot tell which shape is the toy without reading the labels; an actual toy/box illustration would make the scene self-evident.
Wrong-answer explanation ('Yes — look at the rectangle shown: it does') just restates the answer; it should name what to check, e.g. that all four corners are square 90-degree corners.

The correct answer 55° is printed verbatim inside the wedge, so both modes reduce to reading a label and the near-miss distractors (54, 58) test nothing; ask for the scale reading of the second ray, or drop the label.
